parts.text: A student investigated the rate of reaction between zinc and excess hydrochloric acid, at 20 ° C. 2 g of zinc powder was added to 50 cm 3 of dilute hydrochloric acid. The volume of hydrogen released was measured every 30 seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Use the gas syringe diagrams to record the volumes in the table. [3]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot the points on the grid. Draw a smooth line graph. [4]

ms.label: 2(b)

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The experiment was repeated but the hydrochloric acid was cooled to 5 ° C before adding the zinc.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Sketch on the grid the graph you would expect for the results at 5 ° C. Label your graph ‘lower temperature’. [2]

ms.label: 2(d)(ii)
